02_search: Type what you remember. A woman reading a letter: Seurat's drawing, in MoMA's nineteen twenty-nine loan exhibition catalogue, page one twenty-five. The figure, the caption as printed, the record, and a link to the exact page of MoMA's own P.D.F.. Colophon did this for seven hundred and fifty-seven catalogues, seventy-seven thousand pages, with two Meta models.
03_sam: First, SAM three point one finds every picture: paintings, photographs, drawings, prints, sculpture, maps, diagrams. It runs at home, on two DGX Sparks and a forty-ninety, about a page a second per machine. All seventy-seven thousand pages in five hours, zero failures: ninety-three thousand figures.
05_works: A city street at night: Van Gogh's café terrace. And because the captions are read, not guessed, a work can be followed across catalogues. Picasso's Green Still Life, reproduced six times between nineteen thirty-one and nineteen thirty-six, each a different plate. Redon's Silence, five. Say-zann's Bathers, four. Which catalogue reproduced a work, and on which page: that index did not exist.
06_identifier: The identifier reads a book's title page, copyright page and last pages, and returns a catalogue record with the page each field came from. Nothing is guessed: a field not printed comes back empty, with a note.
Every I.S.B.N. is checksum-tested, and a record is verified only when Open Library's title for it matches the title page.

Scored on all seven hundred and fifty-seven catalogues against MoMA's own record sheet, which the model never saw: title ninety-four percent, year ninety, publisher eighty-six, author eighty-five, I.S.B.N. ninety-two.
It even corrects MoMA. This brochure is dated nineteen eighty-seven on the sheet; the copyright line and the exhibition dates say two thousand and five.
